title: Synthetic connect fidelity
blurb: Constructs four synthetic MessageEvent("connect", init) test fakes inside a real SharedWorker and diffs them field by field against the browser-fired connect event.
question: Which MessageEventInit options are required for a synthetic new MessageEvent("connect", init) unit-test fake to match Chrome 160's browser-fired connect event?
result: On Chrome for Testing 153, ports-only and legacy-null fakes matched the real event on every field except isTrusted, spec-shaped ({ data: "" }) differed on data, typeof data, and isTrusted, and no-init differed on ports.length, source === ports[0], and isTrusted. Chrome 160 comparison not verified.
testedIn: Chrome for Testing 153 (legacy null branch verified); not verified in Chrome 160

friction.summary: new MessageEvent("connect") still defaults data to null per MessageEventInit, diverging from the browser-fired empty-string connect event
friction.repro: Construct new MessageEvent("connect", { ports: [port], source: port }) in a unit test; its .data is null rather than "" (and isTrusted is always false).
friction.browser: All browsers (HTML MessageEventInit default vs Chrome 160+/Firefox/Safari UA-fired connect event)
friction.workaround: Pass data: "" explicitly in test fakes ({ data: "", ports: [port], source: port }) and avoid branching on e.isTrusted in code under test.
